lessons.title: Four useful objects
lessons.subtitle: Recognise a book, backpack, chair and clock without typing.

activity.example: el libro = book
la mochila = backpack
la silla = chair
el reloj = clock

cards.question: Match the two labels to their pictures.
Match the two labels to their pictures.

lessons.tipNote: Keep el or la attached to the noun for now. Here, reloj means clock; it can also mean watch. A correct choice is one practice result, not permanent mastery.

lessons.title: One object or two
lessons.subtitle: Use four familiar nouns in small quantity phrases.

cards.question: Meet this phrase.
cards.correctAnswer: Uno = one. Un libro = a/one book. Una mochila = a/one backpack.

activity.example: Uno = one. Un libro = a/one book. Una mochila = a/one backpack.

cards.question: Meet this phrase.
cards.correctAnswer: Dos = two. Dos libros = two books. Dos mochilas = two backpacks.

activity.example: Dos = two. Dos libros = two books. Dos mochilas = two backpacks.

cards.question: Choose the phrase for two books.
Meet this phrase.
cards.correctAnswer: Una silla = a/one chair. Un reloj = a/one clock.

activity.example: Una silla = a/one chair. Un reloj = a/one clock.

cards.question: Meet this phrase.
cards.correctAnswer: Dos sillas = two chairs. Dos relojes = two clocks.

activity.example: Dos sillas = two chairs. Dos relojes = two clocks.

cards.question: Choose the phrase for two chairs.
Your packing list says “dos libros”; choose the quantity.

lessons.tipNote: Uno is one when counting. Before these nouns, use un libro/un reloj and una mochila/una silla. Dos means two. Learn the four forms libros, mochilas, sillas and relojes from the examples. This is not a rule that every noun makes its plural in the same way. Keep optional dragging and tapping equivalent.

lessons.title: A tiny café menu
lessons.subtitle: Recognise three menu meanings and keep earlier object words in use.

cards.question: Meet this word.
cards.correctAnswer: el café = coffee; un café = a coffee

activity.example: el café = coffee; un café = a coffee
la leche = milk

cards.question: Meet this word.
cards.correctAnswer: el bocadillo = filled bread sandwich; un bocadillo = a filled bread sandwich

activity.example: el bocadillo = filled bread sandwich; un bocadillo = a filled bread sandwich

cards.question: Match the two labels to their pictures.
The menu shows a filled bread sandwich; choose its Spanish label.

activity.rule: El bocadillo = the filled bread sandwich.

cards.question: Choose the phrase for a coffee.

lessons.tipNote: Café here means the drink or one serving, not a venue. Leche means milk. A bocadillo is a filled bread sandwich. Our picture shows a bread-roll example, not a required shape or filling. The illustration does not establish an ingredient list. Un café and un bocadillo name one serving/item.

por favor

cards.question: Ask for “A coffee, please” using the pieces.

context.goalFeedback: That works in Spanish. Try the requested goal.

lessons.tipNote: Learn the cashier questions as whole phrases. ¿Qué te pongo? means “What can I get you?” Solo means without milk here. Un café, por favor means “A coffee, please.”

lessons.title: Finish the exchange
lessons.subtitle: Short phrases, then a café visit.

activity.example: para aquí = for here
para llevar = to go / takeaway
¿Para aquí o para llevar? = For here or to go?

cards.question: Match each option to its meaning.

activity.rule: Keep para with both service options.

cards.question: Meet two polite replies.
cards.correctAnswer:
Para aquí, por favor.
Para llevar, por favor.
cards.hint:
For here, please.
To go, please.

activity.example:
Para aquí, por favor. = For here, please.
Para llevar, por favor. = To go, please.

cards.question: What does “¿Para aquí o para llevar?” ask?

activity.rule: This question chooses here or takeaway.

cards.question: Meet the offer of anything else.

activity.example: ¿Algo más? = Anything else?

cards.question: Meet a polite way to decline.

activity.example: No, gracias. = No, thank you.

context.goalFeedback: That works in Spanish. Try the requested goal.

activity.rule: Para llevar matches the takeaway goal.

activity.example: Gracias. = Thank you.

cards.question: Meet two fictional price amounts.
cards.correctAnswer:
un euro
dos euros
Son dos euros.
cards.hint:
1 €: one euro
2 €: two euros
That’s two euros.

activity.example:
un euro = 1 €: one euro
dos euros = 2 €: two euros
Son dos euros. = That’s two euros.

context.goalFeedback: That works in Spanish. Try the requested goal.

activity.rule: No, gracias closes the order without extras.

activity.example: Aquí tienes. = Here you are.

cards.question: Choose the amount in “Son dos euros.”

activity.example: Hasta luego. = See you / goodbye.

cards.question: Choose “Here you are” while handing over payment.
Say you will have the coffee here.

context.goalFeedback: That works in Spanish. Try the requested goal.

activity.rule: Para aquí keeps the coffee here; por favor is welcome but optional.
Hasta luego is the farewell for this visit.

lessons.tipNote: Para aquí means “for here”; para llevar means “to go.” No, gracias politely declines more. Son dos euros means “That’s two euros.” Aquí tienes means “Here you are” while handing over the pretend payment. All prices here are fictional.
